rules.reason: Tests under a failing beforeAll: Jest 30.5 fails each one with the hook's error, Vitest 5.0 skips them (Track 12 F3). An inherent difference between the two runners, so it has no expiry (DECISIONS D30).
mockReset() on fn(impl): Jest 30.5 leaves an empty function, Vitest 5.0 restores the implementation (Track 12 F3). An inherent difference between the two runners, so it has no expiry (DECISIONS D30).

The .snap file each runner writes: header, key and hint joins, and the thrown-error format differ (`// Jest Snapshot v1`, `a b 1`, `"kaboom"` against `// Vitest Snapshot v1`, `a > b 1`, `[Error: kaboom]`; Track 12 F3). An inherent difference between the two runners, so it has no expiry (DECISIONS D30).

An error the runner makes itself, with no frame in one runner: for a thrown string (`thrown: "a string"`) and a test.failing that passed, Jest 30.5 gives the error the stack captured where the test was defined, so its user frame is the test's own call, and Vitest 5.0 has none (a string has no stack, and `Expect test to fail` is made inside the runner). Only a user-frame diff where Vitest has no frame. No policy key names this yet. An inherent difference between the two runners, so it has no expiry (DECISIONS D30).
